title: Rapid and Reproducible Electron Tomography of Chemistry and Structure
content: Three-dimensional (3D) characterization across the nanoscale is now possible using scanning / transmission electron microscopes (S/TEM) [1-3]. Unfortunately, tomographic reconstruction quality and interpretation is bottlenecked by slow data acquisition, reconstruction methods, and visualization. Furthermore, advanced reconstruction techniques, such as chemical or atomic reconstructions, require additional oversight. Even when a final 3D reconstruction is complete, visualization of the same dataset can deviate notably between different laboratories [4]. Achieving high-throughput electron tomography requires an integrated pipeline that links the microscope hardware to optimized reconstruction algorithms and efficient 3D volumetric visualization. Moreover, this pipeline should be multi-threaded to run dynamic visualizations that update as new data is collected or reconstruction algorithms proceed. Lastly, we seek complete reproducibility where preprocessing, reconstruction, and especially visualization are easily transferable between labs.
